title: Leeds’ Anton Stach earns Germany recall, four years after last appearance
content:
Leeds United’s Anton Stach has been called up for Germany’s March friendlies, four years after his last international appearance.

The 27-year-old midfielder has been a key player for the Premier League side this season, after arriving from Hoffenheim last summer.

Stach has proven an asset in defence and attack for the Elland Road outfit, even scoring three direct free kicks this season, including a goal-of-the-season contender at Aston Villa. He will now hope to force his way into Julian Nagelsmann’s World Cup squad this summer.

Speaking about Stach’s inclusion at a press conference on Thursday, Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “It’s well deserved because Anton plays in the best league in the world and this is with unbelievable consistency. His data’s on the top level.

“He has played and adapted also to English football from the first day he arrived. Normally, many players who come to the UK to play for the first time on this level need a bit of time to adapt to the physicality and the intensity.

“Not Anton. He was outstanding and fully deserves this call-up. His all-round game is very, very important for us, in terms of winning balls, against the ball he always puts a shift in and covers lots of distance, wins many duels.

“One thing I can guarantee is Julian will get a top-class character and also a guy who will travel with confidence. I hope he can grip this chance with both hands and fingers crossed for him.”

Stach has played twice for Germany, with both appearances coming in 2022 under Hansi Flick. His debut was against Israel in March of that year, before a three-minute cameo against Italy three months later.

Analysis by Germany correspondent Sebastian Stafford-Bloor

This has been a shock. Previously, Nagelsmann has said that he preferred the role Stach played for Hoffenheim, as the central player in a back-three, rather than the No 6 role he occupies for Leeds.

Stach, Nagelsmann said, was someone “who preferred to have the game in front of him”. He also, confusingly, commented on Stach’s perceived weaknesses in the air and in the tackle, which are criticisms that Premier League fans who have watched him play for Leeds this season will doubtless disagree with.

But the door has been opened. Germany have few midfielders of Stach’s profile. So much so that there has been plenty of support for the return of a player who has been in the international wilderness for nearly four years.

Can he make the World Cup? His scarcity might be his ticket. Leon Goretzka is also in the squad and he can do vaguely similar things, but Emre Can will miss the tournament with a serious knee injury and there is definitely a need to fill the gap he’s left.
